title: Async embed harvest job with semantic batching and global idempotency
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our current bulk/stream embedding intake patterns struggle with mixed-length payloads and cause suboptimal batching and uneven GPU utilization. Clients also need robust at-least-once semantics for large imports and predictable deduplication when retrying. This ticket proposes a new async "harvest" ingestion job that accepts a single job submission (optional client job id) and a streaming or multipart archive of records. The server will perform 'semantic batching' (group by estimated token length and model compatibility) and commit embeddings in append-only, checkpointed slices. Key goals: improve token packing efficiency -> lower cost per embedding; provide simple client retry semantics using a global job id + per-record idempotency; expose job lifecycle and observability for troubleshooting.
acceptance_criteria: API: /v1/embeds/jobs - create job returns server_job_id and accepts optional client_job_id (string)
API: /v1/embeds/jobs/{id}/upload supports streaming multipart or single-file ndjson, responds with per-record temporary ids and final commit token
Idempotency: re-submitting same client_job_id or per-record idempotency_key must not create duplicate final embeddings within a 7-day dedup window
Batching: server groups records into semantic batches (length + model affinity) and achieves at least 20% better tokens-per-GPU compared to naive fixed-size batching on representative workload
Retries: transient failures during commit must be retried with exponential backoff and job must be resumable from last checkpoint
Observability: Console shows job progress, per-batch latency distribution, retry counts, and dedup rate. Telemetry emitted to /metrics and traces for every commit slice
Clients: provide example SDK method in JS and Python with sample retry flow and recommended idempotency key (sha256 of normalized text)
steps: Design API surface and propose JSON schema - link to design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Async+Embedding+Harvest
Implement server_job table with id, client_job_id, status, last_checkpoint, metrics
Add multipart streaming handler that validates ndjson, computes content-hash id per record, and stores to temporary staging bucket
Implement semantic batching engine: token estimator, affinity scoring, and batching policy config (min_fill, max_seq_len, target_tokens_per_batch)
Implement commit worker that reads staged batches, runs embedding model, writes to embeddings store with atomic slice commits and updates job checkpoint
Idempotency: accept client-supplied per-record idempotency_key OR compute sha256(normalize(record.text)) and use as dedupe key
Add retry/backoff logic with a visibility timeout for in-flight slices and a reconciliation worker to recover stuck slices
Add instrumentation (Prometheus metrics + tracing) and Console integration for Job detail view
Write SDK helpers and end-to-end tests with simulated network failures
Run load test against staging with realistic corpus and iterate on batching heuristics
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial write-up and proposal posted. See Confluence design (link above). Proposed semantic batching rather than fixed window to improve GPU packing for varied docs.
2026-03-11 Ravi Patel: Spike results attached: /dashboards/job/semibatch-spike shows 22% improvement on our synthetic news+legal mix. Will iterate on target_tokens_per_batch values.

2026-03-12 PM review (Alex Rivera): PM asked for explicit guarantees around dedup window and storage cost of staging. Decision: 7-day dedup window by default with configurable TTL; staging will be auto-pruned after commit or TTL expiry.
2026-03-13 Design review (Priya Singh): UX for Console job page approved; requested an explicit 'cancel job' path that works even if some slices committed. Added to steps.

2026-03-14 Eng review (Ravi Patel): Implemented a draft handler and opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/13408. Needs infra support for temporary bucket encryption; security team flagged KMS usage.

2026-03-14 Security note (John O'Neill): Because clients may include PII in source text, ensure staging buckets use customer encryption keys when provided and redact logs. Marked security_review_required=true.
notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) Full content de-dup vs client-supplied keys. Chosen design accepts client idempotency keys but falls back to server computed hash to protect naive clients. This balances performance and safety.
Edge cases: Very large single documents (>1M tokens) will be rejected at upload time with clear error and guidance to chunk on client side.
Observability: recommend adding job-level sampling of input records (1%) to preserve repro on failures without logging entire payloads.
Operational runbook: add 'force-commit' and 'roll-forward' operations for support to handle long stuck jobs; link to runbook draft: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/embeddings/harvest-runbook
